verdict.rationale: Unleash documents activation strategies that enable or disable features for certain users without redeploying. Its own example grants access to internal users alongside a percentage rollout, and Edge docs confirm targeting rules use user IDs, emails or IPs. Reusable segments of constraints support named groups such as beta testers. The dated, vague community remark about limited rule flexibility is not a concrete counter-example. missing for 10: explicit documentation of excluding specific users (deny-list or NOT_IN operators), detailed docs of the userId/email constraint mechanics, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can target or exclude specific individual users for a flag (allowlists, beta testers, internal accounts)

citations.quote: They allow you to enable and disable features for certain users without having to redeploy your application.
to roll out a feature to 75% of users while granting access to internal users, you can add two activation strategies
user data (PII) used for targeting rules (like user IDs, emails, or IPs) is processed within the Edge node
A segment is a reusable collection of strategy constraints... you can define a segment once and reuse it across any number of feature flags
